results.claim: Two Saffire-II silicone samples that burned completely in the 1-g test show a burn length of about 0 in microgravity.

results.claim: The Saffire-II SIBAL sample burned 29 cm in microgravity; the 1-g test burned the whole sample.

results.title: At one atmosphere, methanol droplets ignited and burned for some time in 13% oxygen with the rest nitrogen.
results.claim: At one atmosphere, methanol droplets ignited and burned for some time in 13% oxygen with the rest nitrogen.
results.quote: At one atmosphere pressure, ignition and some burning were observed for an oxygen concentration of 13% with the rest being nitrogen.

results.title: For the reported 30% hydrogen / 15% methane / 55% helium blend issuing into 30% oxygen / 70% helium, elevated oxygen facilitated ignition and reduced characteristic flame size; the 5-16.5 cc/s flames expanded to oscillatory radiative extinction.
results.claim: For the reported 30% hydrogen / 15% methane / 55% helium blend issuing into 30% oxygen / 70% helium, elevated oxygen facilitated ignition and reduced characteristic flame size; the 5-16.5 cc/s flames expanded to oscillatory radiative extinction.
results.quote: Test day 20142 investigates the fuel blend 30% H2 / 15% CH4 / 55% He issuing into 30% O2/ 70% He. Elevated oxygen ambient facilitates ignition and results in smaller characteristic flame size. For 5-16.5 cc/s flow rates, flames expand to wavy/oscillatory radiative extinction. Ramp down cases did not allow for assessment of kinetic extinction.

results.title: BRE reports continued combustion without air flow in elevated-oxygen atmospheres, versus short-time self-extinction at 21% oxygen; the source explicitly calls the results preliminary.
results.claim: BRE reports continued combustion without air flow in elevated-oxygen atmospheres, versus short-time self-extinction at 21% oxygen; the source explicitly calls the results preliminary.
results.quote: The ongoing combustion without air flow was notably seen in elevated-oxygen atmospheres which are being considered for use in future spacecraft, whereas such flames in a normal atmosphere of 21% oxygen self-extinguished in a short time. While BRE’s results are still preliminary, they suggest that NASA may want to increase use of its alternative flammability Test 2, with the cone calorimeter, where that test can measure material properties corresponding to the microgravity flames observed with the BRE burner.

results.title: All BRE flames ignited in a normal atmosphere self-extinguished within 40 s, while oxygen mole fractions of 0.265 and above gave quasi-steady flames.
results.claim: All BRE flames ignited in a normal atmosphere self-extinguished within 40 s, while oxygen mole fractions of 0.265 and above gave quasi-steady flames.
results.quote: All flames ignited in normal atmosphere self-extinguished within 40 s. In contrast, oxygen mole fractions of 0.265 and above resulted in quasi-steady flames.

results.title: Quasi-steady burning on a flat surface can exist in microgravity, and ambient oxygen mole fraction plays the most significant role in whether it does.
results.claim: Quasi-steady burning on a flat surface can exist in microgravity, and ambient oxygen mole fraction plays the most significant role in whether it does.
results.quote: It is found out that quasi-steady burning on a flat surface, representing a pool fire, can exist in microgravity. Ambient oxygen mole fraction plays the most significant role in this regard.

results.title: Methane/nitrogen BRE flames self-extinguished within a minute in every ambient condition tested, which indicates that burn time depends on fuel chemistry.
results.claim: Methane/nitrogen BRE flames self-extinguished within a minute in every ambient condition tested, which indicates that burn time depends on fuel chemistry.
results.quote: Methane nitrogen-generated flames self-extinguished within a minute for all ambient conditions. That indicates that the burn time depends on the fuel chemistry.

results.title: In BRE, low-momentum microgravity flames could burn for minutes without air flow, but self-extinguished below about 25% oxygen by volume. At elevated oxygen, larger flames generally self-extinguished within 1.5 minutes, and methane flames within a minute, while smaller or ethylene flames could burn for minutes.
results.claim: In BRE, low-momentum microgravity flames could burn for minutes without air flow, but self-extinguished below about 25% oxygen by volume. At elevated oxygen, larger flames generally self-extinguished within 1.5 minutes, and methane flames within a minute, while smaller or ethylene flames could burn for minutes.
results.quote: Low-momentum microgravity flames can burn for minutes in the absence of an air flow or flame spread. While the flames can burn for minutes in elevated oxygen concentrations, like those being considered for future spacecraft, they were found to self-extinguish in concentrations below ~25% (by volume). While smaller flames can burn for minutes at elevated oxygen concentrations, larger flames were generally seen to self-extinguish within 1.5 minutes. While ethylene flames at elevated oxygen concentrations can burn for minutes, methane flames were seen to self-extinguish within a minute.

results.title: At elevated oxygen concentrations smaller BRE flames could burn for minutes, while larger flames generally self-extinguished within 1.5 minutes.
results.claim: At elevated oxygen concentrations smaller BRE flames could burn for minutes, while larger flames generally self-extinguished within 1.5 minutes.
results.quote: While smaller flames can burn for minutes at elevated oxygen concentrations, larger flames were generally seen to self-extinguish within 1.5 minutes.

results.title: Nitrogen-diluted hydrogen flames seemed to require very large sizes to self-extinguish; radiative extinction was not observed in the cases run despite lower hydrogen concentration, although kinetic extinction appeared during ramp down.
results.claim: Nitrogen-diluted hydrogen flames seemed to require very large sizes to self-extinguish; radiative extinction was not observed in the cases run despite lower hydrogen concentration, although kinetic extinction appeared during ramp down.
results.quote: Nitrogen-diluted hydrogen flames seem to need to be at very large characteristic sizes to self- extinguish. As such, radiative extinction was not observed for the cases run, despite lowering the H2 concentration. However, kinetic extinction during ramp down seem to be exhibited for hydrogen flames.

results.title: Flames of 15% methane / 85% nitrogen ignited but extinguished soon after.
results.claim: Flames of 15% methane / 85% nitrogen ignited but extinguished soon after.
results.quote: For 15% CH4 / 85% N2, flames are ignited, but extinguish soon after.

results.title: The tested rods ignited more slowly near the oxygen limit.
results.claim: In the concurrent rod tests ignition delay rose significantly as the minimum limiting O2 concentration was approached, ignition limits sat at higher O2 than flammability limits, and the delay could be almost 10 times the NASA-STD-6001 standard igniter on time.
results.quote: Ignition delay time increased significantly as the minimum limiting O2 concentration is approached. Ignition limits are found to be at higher O2 concentrations than the flammability limits due to the added heat loss to the initially cold fuel rod present at ignition. The ignition delay time can be up to almost 10 times longer than the NASA STD–6001 standard igniter on time.

results.title: For black PMMA rods in opposed flow, flame spread was observed in microgravity at O2 concentrations as low as 17.5 percent, while in normal gravity it was not observed below 19 percent.
results.claim: For black PMMA rods in opposed flow, flame spread was observed in microgravity at O2 concentrations as low as 17.5 percent, while in normal gravity it was not observed below 19 percent.
results.quote: The most important result of the comparison is that of the minimum O2 concentration for flame spread in normal and microgravity. While in microgravity, flame spread was observed at O2 concentrations as low as 17.5 percent, in normal gravity, flame spread was not observed below 19 percent.

results.title: The three Nomex samples tested in BASS-II did not ignite.
results.claim: The three Nomex samples tested in BASS-II did not ignite.
results.quote: The three Nomex® samples did not ignite, which is an excellent result for fire safety aboard the ISS.

results.title: The preliminary SPICE findings in the 30-day report included in the SLICE final report say the smoke points were consistent with SPICE-1, the potential propane anomaly was not observed, and the trends agreed with 1g although quantitative values were very different.
results.claim: The preliminary SPICE findings in the 30-day report included in the SLICE final report say the smoke points were consistent with SPICE-1, the potential propane anomaly was not observed, and the trends agreed with 1g although quantitative values were very different.
results.quote: Thus far, the SPICE results show that the smoke points for these conditions are consistent with those from SPICE-1. The potential anomalous result seen in SPICE- 1 for propane was not observed and the smoke point trends are consistent with 1g conditions although the quantitative values are very different.

results.title: Silicone looked less flammable in microgravity than in normal gravity, at least at the flow speeds tested.
results.claim: Silicone looked less flammable in microgravity than in normal gravity, at least at the flow speeds tested.
results.quote: Flammability of silicone in microgravity appears to be reduced compared to normal gravity, at least for the flow speeds tested.

results.title: None of the silicone samples burned: when the igniter was switched off a tiny gas-phase flame remained, did not spread, and quickly went out.
results.claim: None of the silicone samples burned: when the igniter was switched off a tiny gas-phase flame remained, did not spread, and quickly went out.
results.quote: Results were convincing although rather anticlimactic as none of the silicone samples burned. When the igniter was powered off, a tiny gas phase flame remained but did not spread and quickly extinguished.

results.title: The PMMA starter gave an average flame power of 460 W (printed as 460 + 50 W) and, despite this heating load, the Nomex fabric was not ignited.
results.claim: The PMMA starter gave an average flame power of 460 W (printed as 460 + 50 W) and, despite this heating load, the Nomex fabric was not ignited.
results.quote: The average flame power from the PMMA (assuming complete conversion of the fuel) was 460 + 50 W. Despite this significant heating load, the fabric was not ignited.

results.title: The first 1 cm of the Nomex fabric was significantly damaged, the first 5 cm completely blackened, and the rest had a black streak down its center.
results.claim: The first 1 cm of the Nomex fabric was significantly damaged, the first 5 cm completely blackened, and the rest had a black streak down its center.
results.quote: The first 1-cm of the fabric was significantly damaged, the first 5-cm was completely blackened, and the remainder had a black streak down its center.
